q-251865.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the two sets of 6 paired observations shown in the table below.


xi 123 122 121 120125 127
yi 102 111 110 105 106 108

Calculate Sxy.

a
 Sxy=−5
b
 Sxy=4
c
 Sxy=−2
d
 Sxy=1
e
 Sxy=−3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a set of n paired observations x1,x2,…,xn and y1,y2,…,yn, Sxy is the sum of products of the deviations of xi and yi from their respective means, that is Sxy=∑i=1n(xi−x―)(yi−y―).

First, we calculate the sample means x― and y―: x―=123+122+121+120+125+1276=123 y―=102+111+110+105+106+1086=107

Next, we calculate the differences between the xi and x―, yi and y―, and their product.


xi 123 122 121 120125 127
yi 102 111 110 105 106 108
(xi−x―) 0 −1 −2 −3 2 4
(yi−y―) −5 4 3 −2 −1 1
(xi−x―)(yi−y―) 0 −4 −6 6 −2 4

Therefore, Sxy is Sxy=0+(−4)+(−6)+6+(−2)+4=−2.

Question 2
?

Consider the two sets of 7 paired observations shown in the table below.




xi 2 3 10 96 57
yi 15 21 22 23 26 1716

Calculate Sxx.

a
Sxx=52
b
Sxx=36
c
Sxx=64
d
Sxx=49
e
Sxx=42
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Given a set of n paired observations x1,x2,…,xn and y1,y2,…,yn, Sxx is the sum of the squared deviations of the data xi from the mean x―, that is Sxx=∑i=1n(xi−x―)2.

First, we calculate the sample mean x―: x―=2+3+10+9+6+5+77=6

Next, we calculate the differences between the xi and x―, and their squares.




xi 2 3 10 96 57
yi 15 21 22 23 26 1716
(xi−x―) −4 −3 4 3 0 −1 1
(xi−x―)2 16 9 16 9 0 1 1

Therefore, Sxx is Sxx=16+9+16+9+0+1+1=52.

q-251488.name: Question 3
q-251488.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ ${S}_{yy}$ is the sum of the squared deviations of the data ${y}_{i}$ from the mean $\overset{―}{y},$ that is

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{yy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we calculate the sample mean $\overset{―}{y}:$

$$
\overset{―}{y}=\frac{16+14+23+17+15}{5}=17.
$$

Next, we calculate the differences between the ${y}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}$, and their squares.

| **$\,{x}_{i}\,$** | $5$ | $11$ | $9$ | $12$ | $18$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **$\,{y}_{i}\,$** | $16$ | $14$ | $23$ | $17$ | $15$ |
| **$\,({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})\,$** | $-1$ | $-3$ | $6$ | $0$ | $-2$ |
| **$\,({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2}\,$** | $1$ | $9$ | $36$ | $0$ | $4$ |

Therefore, ${S}_{yy}$ is

$$
{S}_{yy}=1+9+36+0+4=50.
$$

q-251494.name: Question 6
q-251494.problem:
Consider two sets of $25$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{25},$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{25}.$ You are given that

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx}=125,\,{S}_{yy}=37,\,{S}_{xy}=64.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, ${\sigma }_{x}^{2}=$
{{field-1}}.
q-251494.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the variance of ${x}_{i}$ can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{x}^{2} & =\frac{{S}_{xx}}{n},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${S}_{xx}$ is the sum of squared deviations from the mean for the data ${x}_{i}.$

We are given that ${S}_{xx}=125.$ Substituting the given statistic in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{x}^{2} & =\frac{125}{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
